chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a part of his wealth, so he said: 'One from seven. Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: "For it are seven gates; for every gate of them is a portion assigned."'

I said: 'And a man who bequeathed a share (sahm) of his wealth?' He said: 'The share is one from eight.' Then he recited: 'Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy...' until the end of the verse.

key_terms.لَهَا سَبْعَةُ أَبْوَابٍ: For it are seven gates (Quranic reference)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for an ambiguous bequest of 'a part' or 'a share' of wealth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling on ambiguous bequests (*al-wasiyya al-mubhama*), where Imam al-Rida (AS) derives specific fractions from Quranic numerology: 'part' (*juz'*) is interpreted as one-seventh, alluding to the seven gates of Hell in Surah Al-Hijr, while 'share' (*sahm*) is interpreted as one-eighth, mirroring the eight categories of zakat recipients in Surah At-Tawbah. This demonstrates the Shia jurisprudential method of using Quranic imagery to resolve legal ambiguities in inheritance and charity.
